study_identification_part.si4_title: Cortical thickness and grey-matter volume anomaly detection in individual MRI scans: Comparison of two methods

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Compare ScanOMetrics anomaly detection using features from FreeSurfer vs DL+DiReCT on OASIS3, assess clinical relevance, speed, and agreement with known AD patterns.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The reference cohort is OASIS3; normative models are built from HC scans within OASIS3.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The OASIS3 dataset ... contains ... T1-weighted MRI scans ... Of the 2′014 HC scans ... normative model ... based on 1′927 scans from 696 non-converting subjects.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper explicitly states that the normative model was built using 1,927 scans from 696 non-converting subjects with CDR=0. After cleaning procedures to remove outliers, the final normative model used 1,828 scans.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Of the 2′014 HC scans, 87 are from 41 subjects that had a mixture of scans with CDR = 0 and CDR ≥ 0.5 ('converters' between normal cognition and suspicion or established impairment). Those scans were excluded from building our normative model, which was therefore based on 1'927 scans from 696 non-converting subjects... The 99 HC scans with large number of anomalies (5.15 %) were removed before our final normative models were built from the of 1′828 remaining HC scans.
rci2_hc_n.location: Romascano2024.pdf.md: Section 2.1. OASIS3 dataset and Section 3.7. Cleaning the normative models

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: AD scans show up to ~20× higher anomaly rates than HCs, with CTh reductions in AD predilection regions; DL+DiReCT is ~15× faster than FreeSurfer with similar patterns.
